question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina (not a center located in a residence), what is the maximum number of children aged 0 to 12 months per staff member in a single-age group?
quote: The staff/child ratios and group sizes for single-age groups of children in centers shall be as follows: Age of Children 0 to 12 Months ... Ratio Staff/Children 1/5
notes: Ratio 1:5 with a maximum group size of 10. Centers that opt into multi-age grouping under .0713(d) use 1:4 (group of 8) for 0 to 36 months. Centers in a residence (.0713(b),(c)) also use 1:5 for 0 to 12 months; the 3-12 capacity version allows three additional school-age children.

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina (not a center located in a residence), what is the maximum number of children per staff member in a single-age group of children aged 3 to 4 years?
quote: The staff/child ratios and group sizes for single-age groups of children in centers shall be as follows: Age of Children 0 to 12 Months 12 to 24 Months 2 to 3 Years 3 to 4 Years ... Ratio Staff/Children 1/5 1/6 1/10 1/15
notes: The table's '3 to 4 Years' band is 1:15 with a maximum group size of 25. When age groups are combined, the ratio for the youngest child applies to the whole group (.0713(a)(1)). Residence-based centers use different tables (.0713(b),(c)).

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina (not a center located in a residence), what is the maximum number of children per staff member in a single-age group of children aged 4 to 5 years?
quote: The staff/child ratios and group sizes for single-age groups of children in centers shall be as follows: Age of Children 0 to 12 Months 12 to 24 Months 2 to 3 Years 3 to 4 Years 4 to 5 Years ... Ratio Staff/Children 1/5 1/6 1/10 1/15 1/20
notes: The table's '4 to 5 Years' band is 1:20 with a maximum group size of 25. Under optional multi-age grouping (.0713(d)), 4 to 6 years is 1:9 with a group of 18.

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina (not a center located in a residence) that uses single-age groups, what is the maximum number of children per staff member for children aged 5 years and older?
quote: The staff/child ratios and group sizes for single-age groups of children in centers shall be as follows: Age of Children 0 to 12 Months 12 to 24 Months 2 to 3 Years 3 to 4 Years 4 to 5 Years 5 Years and Older ... Ratio Staff/Children 1/5 1/6 1/10 1/15 1/20 1/25
notes: '5 Years and Older' is the oldest single-age band: 1:25, maximum group 25. Centers that opt into multi-age grouping (.0713(d)) use 1:19 (group 25) for 6 through 12 years. Residence-based centers: 3 to 13 years is 1:15 (13-15 capacity) or 1:12 (3-12 capacity).

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina (not a center located in a residence), what is the maximum group size for a single-age group of children aged 4 to 5 years?
quote: The staff/child ratios and group sizes for single-age groups of children in centers shall be as follows: Age of Children 0 to 12 Months 12 to 24 Months 2 to 3 Years 3 to 4 Years 4 to 5 Years ... Maximum Group Size 10 12 20 25 25
notes: Group size 25 with a 1:20 ratio. Under optional multi-age grouping (.0713(d)), the 4 to 6 years group maximum is 18.

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina, what is the minimum age a person must be to have responsibility for, or be left in charge of, a group of children?
quote: No one under 18 years of age shall have responsibility for or be left in charge of a group of children.
notes: Lead teachers and teachers must also be 18 (.0710(b)). Exception: a teacher's aide aged 16 or 17 may count in ratio if a credentialed staff person at least 21 is present in the room (.0102 definition of 'Teachers aide').

question: For a licensed child care center in North Carolina, what minimum level of formal education must a child care administrator have under the preservice requirements that apply when the administrator has not met the staff qualifications in G.S. 110-91(8)?
answer: A high school diploma or its equivalent
quote: A child care administrator who has not met the staff qualifications required by G.S. 110-91(8) shall meet the requirements in this Rule prior to exercising any child caring responsibilities as follows: (1) have either a high school diploma or its equivalent
notes: The same rule also requires child care experience or education ((a)(2)) and 2 semester credit hours or 32 clock hours of early childhood program administration training, or one year of administrative experience ((a)(3)). G.S. 110-91(8) itself is a statute and is not in this rulebook.

question: After the first year of employment, how many clock hours of on-going training must a staff member who works with children in a licensed child care center in North Carolina complete each year, if they work 40 or more hours a week and have no child-care-related degree, certificate or diploma, no North Carolina Early Childhood Credential, and less than 10 years of documented experience?
quote: shall participate in on-going training activities annually, as follows ... If none of the other criteria in this chart apply ... 20 clock hours
notes: Hours depend on education: 5 (four-year degree), 8 (two-year degree or NC Early Childhood Administration Credential), 10 (certificate/diploma or NC Early Childhood Credential), 15 (10 years documented experience), 20 (none of these). Staff working under 40 hours a week may prorate (.1103(d)). CPR and First Aid do not count (.1103(c)).

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina initially licensed on or after February 1, 1985, a room may not be occupied by more than one child per how many square feet of floor space?
quote: No room may be occupied by more than one child per 25 square feet of floor space
notes: A larger group may use a room for special activities if fire code occupancy is not exceeded. Per .1401(h), the rule applies only to centers initially licensed on or after February 1, 1985. Closets, hallways, kitchens, bathrooms etc. are excluded from Primary Space (.1401(e)).

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina initially licensed after April 1, 1984, what is the minimum outdoor play area required for each child using the outdoor learning environment at any one time?
quote: The outdoor play area shall be no smaller than 75 square feet for each child using the outdoor learning environment at any one time.
notes: Measured per child using the outdoor area at one time, not per licensed capacity. Applies only to centers initially licensed after April 1, 1984 (.1402(b)).

question: Before a licensed child care center in North Carolina may give a child any prescription or over-the-counter medication, what must it have from the child's parent?
answer: Written authorization from the child's parent
quote: No prescription or over-the-counter medication and no topical, non-medical ointment, repellent, lotion, cream, fluoridated toothpaste, or powder shall be administered to any child: (a) without written authorization from the child's parent;
notes: The center also needs written instructions from the parent, physician or other health professional (.0803(1)(b)).

question: How often must fire drills be practiced in a licensed child care center in North Carolina?
quote: Fire drills shall be practiced monthly and records shall be maintained as required by 10A NCAC 09 .0302(d)(5).
notes: Separately, a shelter-in-place or lockdown drill must be held at least every three months (.0604(u)).

question: For how long after a medication is administered must a licensed child care center in North Carolina keep the records of that medication's administration?
quote: Records regarding administration of medications required by Rules .0302(d)(7) and .0803(13) of this Chapter shall be maintained during the time period the medication is being administered and for six months after the medication is administered.
notes: Kept during the period the medication is given plus six months. Other retention periods in the same rule: fire, sanitation and pool inspections at least three years; many child records for as long as the child is enrolled or one year after.

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina, in what position must a caregiver place a child aged 12 months or younger for sleeping, absent a written waiver?
quote: A caregiver shall place a child age 12 months or younger on the child's back for sleeping
notes: Waiver: for a child 6 months or younger, only from a health care professional; for a child older than 6 months, from a health care professional or parent.

question: When a child injured in an incident at a licensed child care center in North Carolina requires medical treatment by a health care professional, community clinic, or local health department, within how many days must a copy of the incident report be mailed to the Division?
quote: When medical treatment is required by a health care professional, community clinic, or local health department as a result of an incident occurring while the child is in care, a copy of the incident report shall be mailed to a representative of the Division within seven calendar days after the incident.
notes: Report goes to the licensing agency (the Division). An incident report must be completed for every injury and signed by the parent (.0802(e)), but no other deadline is set for that.

question: Which staff in a licensed child care center in North Carolina must complete CPR certification appropriate to the ages of the children in care?
answer: All staff who provide direct care or accompany children off premises (and at least one CPR-trained staff member must be present whenever children are in care)
quote: All staff who provide direct care or accompany children when they are off premises shall successfully complete certification in a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course appropriate to the ages of children in care. At all times when children are in care one staff member present must have successfully completed CPR training.
notes: The same staff must also be certified in First Aid (.1102(c)). New staff hired on or after September 1, 2017 must complete the training within 90 days of employment; distance learning is not allowed.

question: When a new child care center opens in North Carolina, the Division issues a temporary license. How long does that temporary license remain in effect, unless a star-rated or other license, suspension or denial comes first?
quote: The temporary license shall remain in effect for six months or until the issuance of a star-rated license, a special provisional license, provisional license, probationary license, summary suspension, suspension, or a denial of a rated license to the operator.
notes: Applies to new centers or a change of owner or location. No expiration or renewal period is stated for the regular star-rated license; a probationary license may last up to 12 months (.2205).

question: During nap time in a licensed child care center in North Carolina, for a group of children aged two years or older, how many staff must remain in the room for the required staff/child ratio to be considered met, assuming all children are visible to that person and the total required staff are on the premises within calling distance?
quote: For groups of children aged two years or older, the staff/child ratio during nap time shall comply with the requirements of this Chapter if at least one person remains in the room, all children are visible to that person, and the total number of required staff are on the premises
notes: Applies only to groups aged two and older; infant/toddler groups get no nap-time relief.

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina that uses single-age groups, during what part of the day may children of all ages be cared for together in one group, and which ratio must then be met?
answer: During the first and last operating hour of the day, keeping the ratio for the youngest child in the group
quote: children of all ages may be cared for together in groups for the first and last operating hour of the day, provided the staff/child ratio for the youngest child in the group is maintained;
notes: At other times, children under one may not be grouped with children two and over, and 12-24 month olds may be grouped with older children only if all are under three (.0713(a)(5),(6)).

question: If a licensed child care center in North Carolina chooses multi-age grouping under 10A NCAC 09 .0713(d) instead of single-age groups, what is the maximum number of children per staff member in a multi-age group of children 0 to 36 months?
quote: The staff/child ratios and group sizes for multi-age groups of children in centers shall be as follows: Age of Children 0 to 36 months ... Ratio Staff/Children 1/4
notes: Stricter than the single-age infant ratio (1:5): multi-age 0 to 36 months is 1:4 with a maximum group of 8. The operator must notify the Division in writing before using multi-age ratios.

question: In a licensed child care center in North Carolina, what is the minimum age at which a teacher's aide may be counted in the staff/child ratio?
quote: A teacher's aide shall be at least 16 years old and less than 18 years old, shall be literate, and may count in staff/child ratio as long as there is also a credentialed staff person who is at least 21 years of age present in the room
notes: Only while a credentialed staff person aged 21 or older is present in the room. Otherwise no one under 18 may be in charge of a group (.0703(a)).

question: Under the safe sleep policy required of a licensed child care center in North Carolina that cares for infants, how often must caregivers visually check, in person, sleeping infants aged 12 months or younger?
quote: specifies that caregivers shall visually check, in person, sleeping infants aged 12 months or younger at least every 15 minutes;
notes: At least every 15 minutes. Documentation of these checks must be kept at least one month (.0606(g)).
